"""
Adım 3 — Standart modellerle karşılaştırma.

Kullanım:
    python 3_comparing_standard_models.py

Her model bir kez eğitilir ve CodeCarbon ile ölçülür (emissions/emissions.csv). Eğitim ve
ölçüm kodu kendi CNN'imizle aynıdır (train_utils.run_experiment). Sonuç diskte varsa yeniden
eğitilmez; yeniden eğitmek için models/<koşu adı>_summary.json silinir.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import os
from datetime import datetime

import pandas as pd
import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.utils.flop_counter import FlopCounterMode
from torchvision.models import (resnet18, ResNet18_Weights,
                                mobilenet_v3_large, MobileNet_V3_Large_Weights)

from data_utils import ROOT, SPLITS_CSV, print_section, print_table
from train_utils import (MODEL_DIR, BATCH_SIZE, MAX_EPOCHS, LEARNING_RATE, WEIGHT_DECAY,
                         EARLY_STOP_PATIENCE, run_experiment, train_mean_age)

# Görüntü boyutu politikası: tüm modeller (kendi CNN'imiz dahil) aynı 64x64 girişi kullanır.
# Böylece modeller arasındaki hata ve enerji farkı yalnızca mimariden ve ön eğitimden gelir.
INPUT_SIZE = 64


class AgeRegressor(nn.Module):
    """Bir backbone'u yaş regresyonuna uyarlar: (N, 3, H, W) -> (N,) yaş (yıl)."""

    def __init__(self, backbone):
        super().__init__()
        self.backbone = backbone

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.backbone(x).squeeze(1)  # (N, 1) -> (N,)


def regression_head(in_features):
    """Tek çıkışlı Linear katman; bias train yaş ortalamasıyla başlar (kendi CNN'imizdeki gibi)."""
    head = nn.Linear(in_features, 1)
    nn.init.constant_(head.bias, train_mean_age())
    return head


def complexity(model, input_size=INPUT_SIZE):
    """Parametre sayısını ve görüntü başına MACs değerini (PyTorch FLOP sayacıyla) döndürür."""
    model.eval()
    with FlopCounterMode(display=False) as counter, torch.no_grad():
        model(torch.zeros(1, 3, input_size, input_size))
    return sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()), counter.get_total_flops() // 2


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Büyük bir model eğit (ResNet-18/50, ConvNeXt-Tiny vb.).
# =====================================================================================
# Seçilen: ResNet-18, ImageNet ağırlıklarından fine-tune (torchvision IMAGENET1K_V1).
# - Neden ResNet-18: "büyük model" sınıfının CPU'da eğitilebilir en küçük standart temsilcisi.
#   11.2 M parametreyle kendi CNN'imizden (~0.29 M) yaklaşık 38 kat büyüktür; ResNet-50 (25.6 M)
#   veya ConvNeXt-Tiny (28.6 M) bu makinede (GPU yok) saatler sürer ve çok daha fazla enerji harcar.
# - Mimari değiştirilmez (standart model olarak kalsın): yalnızca son katman (fc, 1000 sınıf)
#   tek çıkışlı bir regresyon head'iyle değiştirilir.
# - 64x64 girişte ResNet'in stem'i (stride-2 conv + max pool) ve sonraki aşamalar haritayı
#   2x2'ye indirir; bu, ortak görüntü boyutu politikasının bilinen bir bedelidir.
# - Eğitim ayarları (kayıp, optimizer, lr, schedule, augmentation, durdurma) kendi CNN'imizle
#   aynıdır. Giriş normalizasyonu da aynıdır (train setinden hesaplanır); ImageNet istatistikleri
#   yerine bunu kullanmak, BN katmanları fine-tune sırasında uyum sağladığı için kabul edilebilir.
# - Ağırlık indirme işlemi model kurulurken, enerji ölçümü başlamadan önce yapılır.

RESNET_RUN = "resnet18_imagenet_64"


def build_resnet18():
    """ImageNet ağırlıklı ResNet-18 + regresyon head'i."""
    backbone = resnet18(weights=ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1)
    backbone.fc = regression_head(backbone.fc.in_features)  # 512 -> 1
    return AgeRegressor(backbone)


def train_resnet18():
    """ResNet-18'in boyutunu raporlar, sonra modeli eğitir ve ölçer (veya kayıtlı sonucu okur)."""
    parameters, macs = complexity(build_resnet18())
    print(f"ResNet-18 (giriş {INPUT_SIZE}x{INPUT_SIZE}): {parameters:,} parametre, "
          f"{macs / 1e6:.1f} M MACs / görüntü")
    return run_experiment(RESNET_RUN, build_resnet18, INPUT_SIZE)


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Verimlilik odaklı bir model eğit (MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B0, ShuffleNetV2 vb.).
# =====================================================================================
# Seçilen: MobileNetV3-Large, ImageNet ağırlıklarından fine-tune (torchvision IMAGENET1K_V1).
# Adayların 64x64 girişteki maliyeti (1000 sınıflı orijinal head ile, FlopCounterMode):
#     Model               Parametre   MACs / görüntü
#     MobileNetV3-Small   2.54 M       6.5 M
#     MobileNetV3-Large   5.48 M      21.4 M   <- seçilen
#     ShuffleNetV2 x1.0   2.28 M      12.8 M
#     EfficientNet-B0     5.29 M      33.2 M
#     (ResNet-18         11.69 M     148.6 M,  kendi CNN'imiz 0.29 M, 53.7 M)
# - Neden MobileNetV3-Large: MACs'i kendi CNN'imizin ~%40'ı, ResNet-18'in ~1/7'si; böylece üç model
#   net biçimde farklı maliyet seviyelerinde olur. Small daha ucuzdur ama yaş için gereken ince
#   yüz ayrıntılarında kapasitesi sınırlı kalabilir. EfficientNet-B0 daha pahalıdır ve CPU'da yavaş
#   çalışan SiLU aktivasyonu kullanır.
# - Verimlilik fikri: depthwise separable konvolüsyonlar (kanal başına 3x3 + 1x1 karıştırma),
#   inverted residual bloklar ve squeeze-excitation; aynı işi çok daha az MAC ile yapar.
# - Uyarı: depthwise konvolüsyonlar CPU'da bellek erişimiyle sınırlıdır; bu yüzden gerçek süre ve
#   enerji MACs kadar azalmayabilir. Bu fark ölçümle (CodeCarbon) görülecektir.
# - Mimari değiştirilmez; yalnızca classifier'ın son Linear katmanı (1280 -> 1000) tek çıkışlı
#   regresyon head'iyle değiştirilir. Eğitim ayarları ve giriş boyutu diğer modellerle aynıdır.

MOBILENET_RUN = "mobilenetv3_large_imagenet_64"


def build_mobilenet_v3_large():
    """ImageNet ağırlıklı MobileNetV3-Large + regresyon head'i."""
    backbone = mobilenet_v3_large(weights=MobileNet_V3_Large_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1)
    backbone.classifier[-1] = regression_head(backbone.classifier[-1].in_features)  # 1280 -> 1
    return AgeRegressor(backbone)


def train_mobilenet_v3_large():
    """MobileNetV3-Large'ın boyutunu raporlar, sonra modeli eğitir ve ölçer (veya kayıtlı sonucu okur)."""
    parameters, macs = complexity(build_mobilenet_v3_large())
    print(f"MobileNetV3-Large (giriş {INPUT_SIZE}x{INPUT_SIZE}): {parameters:,} parametre, "
          f"{macs / 1e6:.1f} M MACs / görüntü")
    return run_experiment(MOBILENET_RUN, build_mobilenet_v3_large, INPUT_SIZE)


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Her ikisinde de classifier head yerine regresyon head koy.
# =====================================================================================
# İki modelde de aynı yöntem: son sınıflandırma katmanı (1000 çıkış) yerine regression_head()
# (tek çıkışlı Linear, bias = train yaş ortalaması) konur ve AgeRegressor çıkışı (N,) yapar.
#     ResNet-18         : fc (512 -> 1000)            -> Linear(512 -> 1)
#     MobileNetV3-Large : classifier[-1] (1280 -> 1000) -> Linear(1280 -> 1)
# Doğrulama: iki model de örnek girişte (N,) boyutunda tek bir yaş tahmini döndürür ve başlangıç
# tahmini train ortalamasına (~33 yıl) yakındır.


# =====================================================================================
# [x] En az birini ImageNet ağırlıklarından fine-tune et (transfer learning).
# =====================================================================================
# İki standart model de ImageNet ağırlıklarından (torchvision IMAGENET1K_V1) fine-tune edilir:
# build_resnet18() ve build_mobilenet_v3_large() weights=...IMAGENET1K_V1 ile kurulur ve tüm
# katmanlar (dondurulmadan) yaş regresyonu için yeniden eğitilir. Kendi CNN'imiz ise sıfırdan
# eğitildiği için karşılaştırma transfer learning'in etkisini de gösterir.


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Pre-training'in geçmişte yarattığı karbon ayak izini tartış.
# =====================================================================================
# Kullandığımız ImageNet ağırlıkları bizim emissions.csv'mizde görünmez ama bedava değildir:
# biri onları bir kez eğitti ve bu enerji harcandı ("gömülü karbon"). Bu ağırlıklar için
# yayınlanmış bir enerji / karbon değeri yoktur, bu yüzden tahmin edilir.
#
# Doğrulanmış bilgiler (kaynaklar):
#   - torchvision eğitim tarifi (references/classification/README.md):
#       "Except otherwise noted, all models have been trained on 8x V100 GPUs"
#       ResNet-18   : 90 epoch (genel tablo ve train.py varsayılanı), batch 32 / GPU
#       MobileNetV3 : "--epochs 600 --opt rmsprop --batch-size 128 ..."
#     README eğitim süresi, enerji veya karbon vermez.
#   - Görüntü başına MACs (224x224): torchvision ağırlık meta verisi (_ops), ResNet-18 1.814 G,
#     MobileNetV3-Large 0.217 G. (64x64'te ölçtüğümüz değerlerle uyumlu: 148 M x (224/64)^2 ≈ 1.81 G.)
#   - MobileNetV3 mimarisi arama ile bulundu (Howard vd., 2019, "Searching for MobileNetV3"):
#       "we use platform-aware NAS to search for the global network structures ...
#        We then use the NetAdapt algorithm to search per layer for the number of filters."
#     Makale arama maliyetini vermez. Aynı arama yöntemini tanıtan MnasNet (Tan vd., 2019):
#       "each architecture search takes 4.5 days on 64 TPUv2 devices ... our controller
#        samples about 8K models during architecture search"
#
# Tahmin yöntemi (yalnızca yayınlanan son eğitim koşusu):
#   eğitim FLOPs = 3 (forward + backward) x 2 (FLOP / MAC) x MACs x görüntü sayısı x epoch
#   GPU-saat     = FLOPs / (GPU kullanım oranı x V100 FP32 tepe hızı) / 3600
#   enerji       = GPU-saat x GPU gücü x PUE (veri merkezi ek yükü)
#   CO2          = enerji x şebekenin karbon yoğunluğu
# Kullanım oranı, PUE ve karbon yoğunluğu bilinmediği için üç senaryo kullanılır.

IMAGENET_TRAIN_IMAGES = 1_281_167
V100_FP32_TFLOPS = 15.7      # NVIDIA V100 tepe FP32 hızı
V100_POWER_KW = 0.300        # V100 SXM2 TDP; sunucunun CPU/RAM gücü dahil değil (alt sınır)

PRETRAINED_MODELS = [
    # (ad, ağırlık, ImageNet epoch sayısı, bizim fine-tune koşumuzun adı)
    ("ResNet-18", ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1, 90, RESNET_RUN),
    ("MobileNetV3-Large", MobileNet_V3_Large_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1, 600, MOBILENET_RUN),
]

PRETRAINING_SCENARIOS = [
    # (ad, GPU kullanım oranı, PUE, karbon yoğunluğu kg CO2 / kWh)
    ("İyimser", 0.40, 1.1, 0.2),
    ("Orta", 0.20, 1.3, 0.4),
    ("Kötümser", 0.10, 1.6, 0.6),
]

MNASNET_SEARCH_DEVICE_HOURS = 4.5 * 24 * 64   # 6912 TPUv2 cihaz-saati (MnasNet makalesi)


def pretraining_estimate(macs_224, epochs, utilization, pue, carbon_intensity):
    """Bir ImageNet ön eğitiminin FLOPs, GPU-saat, kWh ve kg CO2 tahmini."""
    flops = 3 * 2 * macs_224 * IMAGENET_TRAIN_IMAGES * epochs
    gpu_hours = flops / (utilization * V100_FP32_TFLOPS * 1e12) / 3600
    energy_kwh = gpu_hours * V100_POWER_KW * pue
    return flops, gpu_hours, energy_kwh, energy_kwh * carbon_intensity


def load_summary(run_name):
    """Bir koşunun kayıtlı özetini döndürür; koşu henüz yapılmadıysa None."""
    path = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, f"{run_name}_summary.json")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as file:
        return json.load(file)


def report_pretraining_footprint():
    """Ön eğitimin tahmini enerji ve CO2'sini yazdırır ve bizim ölçümlerimizle kıyaslar."""
    rows = [["Model", "Epoch", "Eğitim FLOPs", "Senaryo", "GPU-saat", "Enerji (kWh)", "CO2 (kg)"]]
    middle = {}
    for name, weights, epochs, _ in PRETRAINED_MODELS:
        macs_224 = weights.meta["_ops"] * 1e9
        for scenario, utilization, pue, intensity in PRETRAINING_SCENARIOS:
            flops, gpu_hours, kwh, co2 = pretraining_estimate(macs_224, epochs, utilization, pue, intensity)
            rows.append([name, epochs, f"{flops:.2e}", scenario, f"{gpu_hours:.0f}", f"{kwh:.1f}", f"{co2:.1f}"])
            if scenario == "Orta":
                middle[name] = (kwh, co2)
    print_table("ImageNet ön eğitiminin tahmini ayak izi (yalnızca yayınlanan son koşu):", rows)
    print("\nSenaryo varsayımları (GPU kullanım oranı / PUE / kg CO2 per kWh):")
    for scenario, utilization, pue, intensity in PRETRAINING_SCENARIOS:
        print(f"  {scenario:9s}: %{utilization * 100:.0f} / {pue} / {intensity}")

    # Bizim ölçtüğümüz fine-tune eğitimleriyle kıyas
    rows = [["Model", "Ön eğitim (Orta, kWh)", "Bizim fine-tune (Wh)", "Ön eğitim / fine-tune"]]
    ratios = []
    for name, _, _, run_name in PRETRAINED_MODELS:
        summary = load_summary(run_name)
        if summary is None:
            rows.append([name, f"{middle[name][0]:.1f}", "henüz eğitilmedi", "-"])
        else:
            ratios.append(middle[name][0] * 1000 / summary["train_energy_Wh"])
            rows.append([name, f"{middle[name][0]:.1f}", f"{summary['train_energy_Wh']:.2f}", f"~{ratios[-1]:,.0f}x"])
    print_table("Ön eğitim ile bizim ölçülen fine-tune enerjimizin kıyası:", rows)
    scale = f"~{min(ratios):,.0f}-{max(ratios):,.0f} kat" if ratios else "(fine-tune henüz ölçülmedi)"

    print(f"""
Tartışma:
  1) Ölçek: Orta senaryoda tek bir ImageNet ön eğitimi, bizim bir fine-tune eğitimimizden
     {scale} fazla enerji harcar. Ağırlıkları indirerek bu maliyeti tekrarlamayız;
     yalnızca çok küçük bir fine-tune maliyeti öderiz. Transfer learning'in yeşil tarafı budur.
  2) Bu tahmin bir alt sınırdır. Yalnızca yayınlanan son eğitim koşusunu sayar; hiperparametre
     aramaları, başarısız denemeler ve geliştirme koşuları dahil değildir. Ayrıca yalnızca GPU
     gücü sayılır (sunucunun CPU, RAM ve ağ gücü yok) ve donanım üretiminin karbonu dahil değildir.
  3) "Verimli model" çıkarımda verimlidir, eğitimde değil. MobileNetV3-Large görüntü başına
     ResNet-18'den ~8 kat az MAC yapar ama 90 yerine 600 epoch eğitildiği için toplam eğitim
     hesabı neredeyse aynıdır. Depthwise konvolüsyonlar GPU'yu daha az verimli kullandığından
     ve 600 epoch'luk veri artırma işi CPU'ya yük bindirdiğinden gerçek maliyeti büyük
     olasılıkla kötümser senaryoya daha yakındır.
  4) Mimari aramanın maliyeti ayrıca eklenmelidir. MobileNetV3'ün mimarisi MnasNet tarzı bir
     arama ve NetAdapt ile bulundu. MnasNet makalesine göre tek bir arama 64 TPUv2 cihazında
     4.5 gün sürer: {MNASNET_SEARCH_DEVICE_HOURS:,.0f} cihaz-saat, yani yukarıdaki ağırlık eğitiminin
     GPU-saatinden çok daha fazla. MobileNetV3 makalesi kendi arama maliyetini vermez; bu yüzden
     yalnızca büyüklük mertebesi olarak verilebilir. ResNet ise elle tasarlanmıştır.
  5) Paylaşım (amortisman): ön eğitim bir kez yapılır ve ağırlıklar çok sayıda kişi tarafından
     yeniden kullanılır; kişi başına düşen pay küçüktür. Ancak projenin dürüst karbon raporunda
     emissions.csv toplamının yanında bu gömülü maliyet ayrıca ve tahmin olarak belirtilmelidir.
  6) Belirsizlik büyüktür: senaryolar arasında ~{max_min_ratio():.0f} kat fark vardır. Bu yüzden sonuç tek bir
     sayı olarak değil, bir aralık ve büyüklük mertebesi olarak raporlanmalıdır.""")


def max_min_ratio():
    """Kötümser ve iyimser senaryo CO2 tahminleri arasındaki oran (model fark etmez)."""
    estimates = [pretraining_estimate(1.0, 1, u, p, c)[3] for _, u, p, c in PRETRAINING_SCENARIOS]
    return max(estimates) / min(estimates)


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Tüm modellerde aynı split, aynı görüntü boyutu politikası ve aynı evaluation kodunu kullan.
# =====================================================================================
# Kodla nasıl sağlanıyor:
#   - Aynı split    : her model data/splits.csv'yi data_utils.load_split() ile okur (seed 42,
#                     bir kez üretilip korunur). Test seti yalnızca adım 5'te, load_test_once() ile.
#   - Aynı görüntü  : her model aynı önbellekten (data_utils.load_images) 200x200 -> 64x64
#                     bilinear küçültülmüş görüntüleri ve train'den hesaplanan aynı normalizasyonu alır.
#   - Aynı kod      : her model train_utils.run_experiment() ile eğitilir ve ölçülür: aynı kayıp,
#                     optimizer, lr, schedule, augmentation, durdurma, aynı regression_metrics()
#                     ve aynı CodeCarbon ölçümü. Modele özel olan tek şey build_model fonksiyonudur.
# check_fairness() bunu çalıştırılmış koşular üzerinde doğrular ve sonuçları aynı tabloda gösterir.

COMPARED_RUNS = [
    # (ad, koşu adı, ön eğitim)
    ("Kendi CNN", "own_cnn_64", "yok (sıfırdan)"),
    ("ResNet-18", RESNET_RUN, "ImageNet"),
    ("MobileNetV3-Large", MOBILENET_RUN, "ImageNet"),
]
OWN_CNN_LAYERS_CSV = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "own_cnn_layers.csv")
MODEL_BUILDERS = {RESNET_RUN: build_resnet18, MOBILENET_RUN: build_mobilenet_v3_large}


RUN_NOTES_CSV = os.path.join(ROOT, "emissions", "run_notes.csv")


def measurement_status(run_name):
    """Koşunun özette kullanılan eğitim ölçümünün durumu (emissions/run_notes.csv)."""
    if not os.path.exists(RUN_NOTES_CSV):
        return "not yok (tek başına koşu)"
    notes = pd.read_csv(RUN_NOTES_CSV)
    used = notes[(notes["project_name"] == run_name) & (notes["ozette_kullanilan"] == "evet")]
    if used.empty:
        return "not yok (tek başına koşu)"
    note = used.iloc[-1]
    return f"{note['olcum_durumu']}, {note['guc_modu']}"


def file_fingerprint(path):
    """Dosyanın SHA-256 özetinin ilk 12 karakteri."""
    with open(path, "rb") as file:
        return hashlib.sha256(file.read()).hexdigest()[:12]


def run_macs(run_name):
    """Koşunun modelinin 64x64'te görüntü başına MACs değeri."""
    if run_name in MODEL_BUILDERS:
        return complexity(MODEL_BUILDERS[run_name]())[1]
    return pd.read_csv(OWN_CNN_LAYERS_CSV)["MACs"].sum()  # kendi CNN: adım 2'nin katman tablosu


def check_fairness():
    """Tüm modellerin aynı split, aynı giriş boyutu ve aynı kodla değerlendirildiğini doğrular."""
    split_time = os.path.getmtime(SPLITS_CSV)
    print(f"Split dosyası : {SPLITS_CSV}")
    print(f"  SHA-256     : {file_fingerprint(SPLITS_CSV)}   (tüm modeller bu dosyayı okur)")
    print(f"  Son değişim : {datetime.fromtimestamp(split_time):%Y-%m-%d %H:%M}")
    print(f"Eğitim ayarları (train_utils, tüm modellerde aynı): batch {BATCH_SIZE}, AdamW lr {LEARNING_RATE:g}, "
          f"weight decay {WEIGHT_DECAY:g}, erken durdurma {EARLY_STOP_PATIENCE}. Epoch üst sınırı modele göre "
          f"tabloda (güncel ayar: {MAX_EPOCHS}).")

    rows = [["Model", "Ön eğitim", "Giriş", "Epoch sınırı", "Split eğitimden önce mi?", "Parametre", "MACs (M)",
             "val MAE", "val RMSE", "val R²", "Eğitim (Wh)", "Çıkarım (mWh/1000)", "Enerji ölçümü"]]
    problems, epoch_limits = [], set()
    for name, run_name, pretraining in COMPARED_RUNS:
        summary = load_summary(run_name)
        if summary is None:
            rows.append([name, pretraining, "-", "-", "-", "-", "-", "henüz eğitilmedi", "", "", "", "", ""])
            problems.append(f"{name} henüz eğitilmedi")
            continue

        summary_time = os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, f"{run_name}_summary.json"))
        split_before = summary_time > split_time
        if summary["input_size"] != INPUT_SIZE:
            problems.append(f"{name}: giriş {summary['input_size']} (beklenen {INPUT_SIZE})")
        if not split_before:
            problems.append(f"{name}: split dosyası bu eğitimden sonra değişmiş")

        # "max_epochs" alanı özete sonradan eklendi; alanı olmayan özetlerin hepsi 20 epoch sınırıyla eğitildi.
        epoch_limit = summary.get("max_epochs", 20)
        epoch_limits.add(epoch_limit)
        rows.append([name, pretraining, f"{summary['input_size']}px", epoch_limit,
                     "evet" if split_before else "HAYIR",
                     f"{summary['parameters']:,}", f"{run_macs(run_name) / 1e6:.1f}",
                     f"{summary['val_MAE']:.2f}", f"{summary['val_RMSE']:.2f}", f"{summary['val_R2']:.3f}",
                     f"{summary['train_energy_Wh']:.2f}", f"{summary['infer_mWh_per_1000']:.2f}",
                     measurement_status(run_name)])
    print_table("Aynı split, aynı giriş ve aynı kodla ölçülen sonuçlar (validation):", rows)
    if any(word in row[-1] for row in rows[1:] for word in ("cakis", "uyku", "dusuk")):
        print("\nUyarı: enerji ölçümleri aynı koşullarda alınmadı (çakışan koşular / farklı güç modları);\n"
              f"ayrıntılar {RUN_NOTES_CSV}. Hata metrikleri (val MAE, RMSE, R²) bundan etkilenmez.")

    if len(epoch_limits) > 1:
        problems.append(f"modeller farklı epoch üst sınırlarıyla eğitildi ({sorted(epoch_limits)}); "
                        "eğitim bütçesi eşit değil, raporda belirtilmeli")

    if problems:
        print("\nEksik / uyumsuz:")
        for problem in problems:
            print(f"  - {problem}")
    else:
        print("\nKontrol geçti: tüm modeller aynı split, aynı 64x64 giriş ve aynı eğitim/değerlendirme "
              "koduyla ölçüldü.")


def main():
    print_section("1) Büyük model: ResNet-18 (ImageNet fine-tune)")
    train_resnet18()

    print_section("2) Verimlilik odaklı model: MobileNetV3-Large (ImageNet fine-tune)")
    train_mobilenet_v3_large()

    print_section("3) Ön eğitimin karbon ayak izi")
    report_pretraining_footprint()

    print_section("4) Aynı split, aynı görüntü boyutu ve aynı değerlendirme kodu")
    check_fairness()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
Step 3 — Comparison with standard models.

Usage:
    python 3_comparing_standard_models.py

Each model is trained once and measured with CodeCarbon (emissions/emissions.csv). The training and
measurement code is the same as for our own CNN (train_utils.run_experiment). If the result exists
on disk it is not retrained; to retrain, delete models/<run name>_summary.json.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import os
from datetime import datetime

import pandas as pd
import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.utils.flop_counter import FlopCounterMode
from torchvision.models import (resnet18, ResNet18_Weights,
                                mobilenet_v3_large, MobileNet_V3_Large_Weights)

from data_utils import ROOT, SPLITS_CSV, print_section, print_table
from train_utils import (MODEL_DIR, BATCH_SIZE, MAX_EPOCHS, LEARNING_RATE, WEIGHT_DECAY,
                         EARLY_STOP_PATIENCE, run_experiment, train_mean_age)

# Image size policy: all models (including our own CNN) use the same 64x64 input.
# So the difference in error and energy between models comes only from the architecture and pretraining.
INPUT_SIZE = 64


class AgeRegressor(nn.Module):
    """Adapts a backbone to age regression: (N, 3, H, W) -> (N,) age (years)."""

    def __init__(self, backbone):
        super().__init__()
        self.backbone = backbone

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.backbone(x).squeeze(1)  # (N, 1) -> (N,)


def regression_head(in_features):
    """Single-output Linear layer; the bias starts at the mean train age (as in our own CNN)."""
    head = nn.Linear(in_features, 1)
    nn.init.constant_(head.bias, train_mean_age())
    return head


def complexity(model, input_size=INPUT_SIZE):
    """Returns the parameter count and the MACs per image (with PyTorch's FLOP counter)."""
    model.eval()
    with FlopCounterMode(display=False) as counter, torch.no_grad():
        model(torch.zeros(1, 3, input_size, input_size))
    return sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()), counter.get_total_flops() // 2


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Train a large model (ResNet-18/50, ConvNeXt-Tiny, etc.).
# =====================================================================================
# Chosen: ResNet-18, fine-tuned from ImageNet weights (torchvision IMAGENET1K_V1).
# - Why ResNet-18: the smallest standard representative of the "large model" class that can be trained
#   on a CPU. With 11.2 M parameters it is about 38 times larger than our own CNN (~0.29 M); ResNet-50 (25.6 M)
#   or ConvNeXt-Tiny (28.6 M) would take hours on this machine (no GPU) and consume much more energy.
# - The architecture is not changed (so it stays a standard model): only the last layer (fc, 1000 classes)
#   is replaced with a single-output regression head.
# - With a 64x64 input, ResNet's stem (stride-2 conv + max pool) and the following stages shrink the map
#   to 2x2; this is a known cost of the shared image size policy.
# - The training settings (loss, optimizer, lr, schedule, augmentation, stopping) are the same as for our
#   own CNN. The input normalization is also the same (computed from the train set); using it instead of the
#   ImageNet statistics is acceptable because the BN layers adapt during fine-tuning.
# - The weights are downloaded while the model is built, before the energy measurement starts.

RESNET_RUN = "resnet18_imagenet_64"


def build_resnet18():
    """ResNet-18 with ImageNet weights + regression head."""
    backbone = resnet18(weights=ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1)
    backbone.fc = regression_head(backbone.fc.in_features)  # 512 -> 1
    return AgeRegressor(backbone)


def train_resnet18():
    """Reports the size of ResNet-18, then trains and measures the model (or reads the saved result)."""
    parameters, macs = complexity(build_resnet18())
    print(f"ResNet-18 (input {INPUT_SIZE}x{INPUT_SIZE}): {parameters:,} parameters, "
          f"{macs / 1e6:.1f} M MACs / image")
    return run_experiment(RESNET_RUN, build_resnet18, INPUT_SIZE)


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Train an efficiency-oriented model (MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B0, ShuffleNetV2, etc.).
# =====================================================================================
# Chosen: MobileNetV3-Large, fine-tuned from ImageNet weights (torchvision IMAGENET1K_V1).
# Cost of the candidates at a 64x64 input (with the original 1000-class head, FlopCounterMode):
#     Model               Params      MACs / image
#     MobileNetV3-Small   2.54 M       6.5 M
#     MobileNetV3-Large   5.48 M      21.4 M   <- chosen
#     ShuffleNetV2 x1.0   2.28 M      12.8 M
#     EfficientNet-B0     5.29 M      33.2 M
#     (ResNet-18         11.69 M     148.6 M,  our own CNN 0.29 M, 53.7 M)
# - Why MobileNetV3-Large: its MACs are ~40% of our own CNN's and ~1/7 of ResNet-18's; so the three models
#   are at clearly different cost levels. Small is cheaper, but its capacity may be limited for the fine
#   facial details needed for age. EfficientNet-B0 is more expensive and uses the SiLU activation, which
#   runs slowly on a CPU.
# - The efficiency idea: depthwise separable convolutions (3x3 per channel + 1x1 mixing),
#   inverted residual blocks and squeeze-excitation; they do the same work with far fewer MACs.
# - Caveat: depthwise convolutions are memory-bound on a CPU; therefore the real time and energy may
#   not drop as much as the MACs. This difference will be seen in the measurement (CodeCarbon).
# - The architecture is not changed; only the last Linear layer of the classifier (1280 -> 1000) is
#   replaced with a single-output regression head. Training settings and input size are the same as the other models.

MOBILENET_RUN = "mobilenetv3_large_imagenet_64"


def build_mobilenet_v3_large():
    """MobileNetV3-Large with ImageNet weights + regression head."""
    backbone = mobilenet_v3_large(weights=MobileNet_V3_Large_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1)
    backbone.classifier[-1] = regression_head(backbone.classifier[-1].in_features)  # 1280 -> 1
    return AgeRegressor(backbone)


def train_mobilenet_v3_large():
    """Reports the size of MobileNetV3-Large, then trains and measures the model (or reads the saved result)."""
    parameters, macs = complexity(build_mobilenet_v3_large())
    print(f"MobileNetV3-Large (input {INPUT_SIZE}x{INPUT_SIZE}): {parameters:,} parameters, "
          f"{macs / 1e6:.1f} M MACs / image")
    return run_experiment(MOBILENET_RUN, build_mobilenet_v3_large, INPUT_SIZE)


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Put a regression head instead of the classifier head in both.
# =====================================================================================
# The same method in both models: the last classification layer (1000 outputs) is replaced with
# regression_head() (single-output Linear, bias = mean train age) and AgeRegressor makes the output (N,).
#     ResNet-18         : fc (512 -> 1000)              -> Linear(512 -> 1)
#     MobileNetV3-Large : classifier[-1] (1280 -> 1000) -> Linear(1280 -> 1)
# Check: both models return a single age prediction of shape (N,) for a sample input, and the initial
# prediction is close to the train mean (~33 years).


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Fine-tune at least one of them from ImageNet weights (transfer learning).
# =====================================================================================
# Both standard models are fine-tuned from ImageNet weights (torchvision IMAGENET1K_V1):
# build_resnet18() and build_mobilenet_v3_large() are built with weights=...IMAGENET1K_V1 and all
# layers (none frozen) are retrained for age regression. Since our own CNN is trained from scratch,
# the comparison also shows the effect of transfer learning.


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Discuss the carbon footprint that pretraining created in the past.
# =====================================================================================
# The ImageNet weights we use do not appear in our emissions.csv, but they are not free:
# someone trained them once and that energy was spent ("embodied carbon"). No energy / carbon value
# has been published for these weights, so it is estimated.
#
# Verified facts (sources):
#   - torchvision training recipe (references/classification/README.md):
#       "Except otherwise noted, all models have been trained on 8x V100 GPUs"
#       ResNet-18   : 90 epochs (general table and train.py default), batch 32 / GPU
#       MobileNetV3 : "--epochs 600 --opt rmsprop --batch-size 128 ..."
#     The README gives no training time, energy or carbon.
#   - MACs per image (224x224): torchvision weight metadata (_ops), ResNet-18 1.814 G,
#     MobileNetV3-Large 0.217 G. (Consistent with our 64x64 measurement: 148 M x (224/64)^2 ≈ 1.81 G.)
#   - The MobileNetV3 architecture was found by search (Howard et al., 2019, "Searching for MobileNetV3"):
#       "we use platform-aware NAS to search for the global network structures ...
#        We then use the NetAdapt algorithm to search per layer for the number of filters."
#     The paper does not give the search cost. MnasNet, which introduced the same search method (Tan et al., 2019):
#       "each architecture search takes 4.5 days on 64 TPUv2 devices ... our controller
#        samples about 8K models during architecture search"
#
# Estimation method (only the final published training run):
#   training FLOPs = 3 (forward + backward) x 2 (FLOP / MAC) x MACs x number of images x epochs
#   GPU-hours      = FLOPs / (GPU utilization x V100 FP32 peak throughput) / 3600
#   energy         = GPU-hours x GPU power x PUE (data-center overhead)
#   CO2            = energy x carbon intensity of the grid
# Since utilization, PUE and carbon intensity are unknown, three scenarios are used.

IMAGENET_TRAIN_IMAGES = 1_281_167
V100_FP32_TFLOPS = 15.7      # NVIDIA V100 peak FP32 throughput
V100_POWER_KW = 0.300        # V100 SXM2 TDP; the server's CPU/RAM power is not included (lower bound)

PRETRAINED_MODELS = [
    # (name, weights, number of ImageNet epochs, name of our fine-tuning run)
    ("ResNet-18", ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1, 90, RESNET_RUN),
    ("MobileNetV3-Large", MobileNet_V3_Large_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1, 600, MOBILENET_RUN),
]

PRETRAINING_SCENARIOS = [
    # (name, GPU utilization, PUE, carbon intensity kg CO2 / kWh)
    ("Optimistic", 0.40, 1.1, 0.2),
    ("Central", 0.20, 1.3, 0.4),
    ("Pessimistic", 0.10, 1.6, 0.6),
]

MNASNET_SEARCH_DEVICE_HOURS = 4.5 * 24 * 64   # 6912 TPUv2 device-hours (MnasNet paper)


def pretraining_estimate(macs_224, epochs, utilization, pue, carbon_intensity):
    """Estimate of the FLOPs, GPU-hours, kWh and kg CO2 of one ImageNet pretraining."""
    flops = 3 * 2 * macs_224 * IMAGENET_TRAIN_IMAGES * epochs
    gpu_hours = flops / (utilization * V100_FP32_TFLOPS * 1e12) / 3600
    energy_kwh = gpu_hours * V100_POWER_KW * pue
    return flops, gpu_hours, energy_kwh, energy_kwh * carbon_intensity


def load_summary(run_name):
    """Returns the saved summary of a run; None if the run has not been done yet."""
    path = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, f"{run_name}_summary.json")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as file:
        return json.load(file)


def report_pretraining_footprint():
    """Prints the estimated energy and CO2 of pretraining and compares them with our measurements."""
    rows = [["Model", "Epochs", "Training FLOPs", "Scenario", "GPU-hours", "Energy (kWh)", "CO2 (kg)"]]
    middle = {}
    for name, weights, epochs, _ in PRETRAINED_MODELS:
        macs_224 = weights.meta["_ops"] * 1e9
        for scenario, utilization, pue, intensity in PRETRAINING_SCENARIOS:
            flops, gpu_hours, kwh, co2 = pretraining_estimate(macs_224, epochs, utilization, pue, intensity)
            rows.append([name, epochs, f"{flops:.2e}", scenario, f"{gpu_hours:.0f}", f"{kwh:.1f}", f"{co2:.1f}"])
            if scenario == "Central":
                middle[name] = (kwh, co2)
    print_table("Estimated footprint of ImageNet pretraining (only the final published run):", rows)
    print("\nScenario assumptions (GPU utilization / PUE / kg CO2 per kWh):")
    for scenario, utilization, pue, intensity in PRETRAINING_SCENARIOS:
        print(f"  {scenario:11s}: {utilization * 100:.0f}% / {pue} / {intensity}")

    # Comparison with the fine-tuning trainings we measured
    rows = [["Model", "Pretraining (Central, kWh)", "Our fine-tuning (Wh)", "Pretraining / fine-tuning"]]
    ratios = []
    for name, _, _, run_name in PRETRAINED_MODELS:
        summary = load_summary(run_name)
        if summary is None:
            rows.append([name, f"{middle[name][0]:.1f}", "not trained yet", "-"])
        else:
            ratios.append(middle[name][0] * 1000 / summary["train_energy_Wh"])
            rows.append([name, f"{middle[name][0]:.1f}", f"{summary['train_energy_Wh']:.2f}", f"~{ratios[-1]:,.0f}x"])
    print_table("Pretraining vs. the fine-tuning energy we measured:", rows)
    scale = f"~{min(ratios):,.0f}-{max(ratios):,.0f} times" if ratios else "(fine-tuning not measured yet)"

    print(f"""
Discussion:
  1) Scale: in the central scenario, a single ImageNet pretraining consumes {scale} more energy
     than one of our fine-tuning trainings. By downloading the weights we do not repeat this cost;
     we only pay a very small fine-tuning cost. This is the green side of transfer learning.
  2) This estimate is a lower bound. It counts only the final published training run; hyperparameter

Usage:

Each model is trained once and measured with CodeCarbon (emissions/emissions.csv). The training and

import json

# Image size policy: all models (including our own CNN) use the same 64x64 input.
# So the difference in error and energy between models comes only from the architecture and pretraining.
INPUT_SIZE = 64


class AgeRegressor(nn.Module):
    """Adapts a backbone to age regression: (N, 3, H, W) -> (N,) age (years)."""

    def __init__(self, backbone):
        super().__init__()
        self.backbone = backbone

    def forward(self, x):

    """Single-output Linear layer; the bias starts at the mean train age (as in our own CNN)."""

    return head

    """Returns the parameter count and the MACs per image (with PyTorch's FLOP counter)."""

    split_time = os.path.getmtime(SPLITS_CSV)

    print(f"  SHA-256     : {file_fingerprint(SPLITS_CSV)}   (all models read this file)")
    print(f"  Last change : {datetime.fromtimestamp(split_time):%Y-%m-%d %H:%M}")
    print(f"Training settings (train_utils, identical for all models): batch {BATCH_SIZE}, AdamW lr {LEARNING_RATE:g}, "
          f"weight decay {WEIGHT_DECAY:g}, early stopping {EARLY_STOP_PATIENCE}. The epoch limit per model is "
          f"in the table (current setting: {MAX_EPOCHS}).")

    rows = [["Model", "Pretraining", "Input", "Epoch limit", "Split before training?", "Params", "MACs (M)",
             "val MAE", "val RMSE", "val R²", "Training (Wh)", "Inference (mWh/1000)", "Energy measurement"]]
    problems, epoch_limits = [], set()
    for name, run_name, pretraining in COMPARED_RUNS:
        summary = load_summary(run_name)
        if summary is None:
            rows.append([name, pretraining, "-", "-", "-", "-", "-", "not trained yet", "", "", "", "", ""])
            problems.append(f"{name} not trained yet")
            continue

        summary_time = os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, f"{run_name}_summary.json"))
        split_before = summary_time > split_time
        if summary["input_size"] != INPUT_SIZE:
            problems.append(f"{name}: input {summary['input_size']} (expected {INPUT_SIZE})")
        if not split_before:
            problems.append(f"{name}: the split file changed after this training")

        # The "max_epochs" field was added to the summary later; all summaries without it were trained with a 20-epoch limit.
        epoch_limit = summary.get("max_epochs", 20)
        epoch_limits.add(epoch_limit)
        rows.append([name, pretraining, f"{summary['input_size']}px", epoch_limit,
                     "yes" if split_before else "NO",
                     f"{summary['parameters']:,}", f"{run_macs(run_name) / 1e6:.1f}",
                     f"{summary['val_MAE']:.2f}", f"{summary['val_RMSE']:.2f}", f"{summary['val_R2']:.3f}",
                     f"{summary['train_energy_Wh']:.2f}", f"{summary['infer_mWh_per_1000']:.2f}",
                     measurement_status(run_name)])
    print_table("Results measured with the same split, the same input and the same code (validation):", rows)
    if any(word in row[-1] for row in rows[1:] for word in ("overlapping", "sleep", "low (")):
        print("\nWarning: the energy measurements were not taken under the same conditions (overlapping runs /\n"
              f"different power modes); details in {RUN_NOTES_CSV}. The error metrics (val MAE, RMSE, R²) are not affected.")

    if len(epoch_limits) > 1:
        problems.append(f"the models were trained with different epoch limits ({sorted(epoch_limits)}); "
                        "the training budget is not equal, this must be stated in the report")

    if problems:
        print("\nMissing / inconsistent:")
        for problem in problems:
            print(f"  - {problem}")
    else:
        print("\nCheck passed: all models were measured with the same split, the same 64x64 input and the same "
              "training/evaluation code.")


def main():
    print_section("1) Large model: ResNet-18 (ImageNet fine-tuning)")
    train_resnet18()

    print_section("2) Efficiency-oriented model: MobileNetV3-Large (ImageNet fine-tuning)")
    train_mobilenet_v3_large()

    print_section("3) Carbon footprint of pretraining")
    report_pretraining_footprint()

    print_section("4) Same split, same image size and same evaluation code")
    check_fairness()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
Step 3 — Comparison with standard models.

Usage:
    python 3_comparing_standard_models.py

Each model is trained once and measured with CodeCarbon (emissions/emissions.csv). The training and
measurement code is the same as for our own CNN (train_utils.run_experiment). If the result exists
on disk it is not retrained; to retrain, delete models/<run name>_summary.json.
"""

import hashlib
import json
import os
from datetime import datetime

import pandas as pd
import torch
from torch import nn
from torch.utils.flop_counter import FlopCounterMode
from torchvision.models import (resnet18, ResNet18_Weights,
                                mobilenet_v3_large, MobileNet_V3_Large_Weights)

from data_utils import ROOT, SPLITS_CSV, print_section, print_table
from train_utils import (MODEL_DIR, BATCH_SIZE, MAX_EPOCHS, LEARNING_RATE, WEIGHT_DECAY,
                         EARLY_STOP_PATIENCE, run_experiment, train_mean_age)

# Image size policy: all models (including our own CNN) use the same 64x64 input.
# So the difference in error and energy between models comes only from the architecture and pretraining.
INPUT_SIZE = 64


class AgeRegressor(nn.Module):
    """Adapts a backbone to age regression: (N, 3, H, W) -> (N,) age (years)."""

    def __init__(self, backbone):
        super().__init__()
        self.backbone = backbone

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.backbone(x).squeeze(1)  # (N, 1) -> (N,)


def regression_head(in_features):
    """Single-output Linear layer; the bias starts at the mean train age (as in our own CNN)."""
    head = nn.Linear(in_features, 1)
    nn.init.constant_(head.bias, train_mean_age())
    return head


def complexity(model, input_size=INPUT_SIZE):
    """Returns the parameter count and the MACs per image (with PyTorch's FLOP counter)."""
    model.eval()
    with FlopCounterMode(display=False) as counter, torch.no_grad():
        model(torch.zeros(1, 3, input_size, input_size))
    return sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()), counter.get_total_flops() // 2


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Train a large model (ResNet-18/50, ConvNeXt-Tiny, etc.).
# =====================================================================================
# Chosen: ResNet-18, fine-tuned from ImageNet weights (torchvision IMAGENET1K_V1).
# - Why ResNet-18: the smallest standard representative of the "large model" class that can be trained
#   on a CPU. With 11.2 M parameters it is about 38 times larger than our own CNN (~0.29 M); ResNet-50 (25.6 M)
#   or ConvNeXt-Tiny (28.6 M) would take hours on this machine (no GPU) and consume much more energy.
# - The architecture is not changed (so it stays a standard model): only the last layer (fc, 1000 classes)
#   is replaced with a single-output regression head.
# - With a 64x64 input, ResNet's stem (stride-2 conv + max pool) and the following stages shrink the map
#   to 2x2; this is a known cost of the shared image size policy.
# - The training settings (loss, optimizer, lr, schedule, augmentation, stopping) are the same as for our
#   own CNN. The input normalization is also the same (computed from the train set); using it instead of the
#   ImageNet statistics is acceptable because the BN layers adapt during fine-tuning.
# - The weights are downloaded while the model is built, before the energy measurement starts.

RESNET_RUN = "resnet18_imagenet_64"


def build_resnet18():
    """ResNet-18 with ImageNet weights + regression head."""
    backbone = resnet18(weights=ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1)
    backbone.fc = regression_head(backbone.fc.in_features)  # 512 -> 1
    return AgeRegressor(backbone)


def train_resnet18():
    """Reports the size of ResNet-18, then trains and measures the model (or reads the saved result)."""
    parameters, macs = complexity(build_resnet18())
    print(f"ResNet-18 (input {INPUT_SIZE}x{INPUT_SIZE}): {parameters:,} parameters, "
          f"{macs / 1e6:.1f} M MACs / image")
    return run_experiment(RESNET_RUN, build_resnet18, INPUT_SIZE)


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Train an efficiency-oriented model (MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B0, ShuffleNetV2, etc.).
# =====================================================================================
# Chosen: MobileNetV3-Large, fine-tuned from ImageNet weights (torchvision IMAGENET1K_V1).
# Cost of the candidates at a 64x64 input (with the original 1000-class head, FlopCounterMode):
#     Model               Params      MACs / image
#     MobileNetV3-Small   2.54 M       6.5 M
#     MobileNetV3-Large   5.48 M      21.4 M   <- chosen
#     ShuffleNetV2 x1.0   2.28 M      12.8 M
#     EfficientNet-B0     5.29 M      33.2 M
#     (ResNet-18         11.69 M     148.6 M,  our own CNN 0.29 M, 53.7 M)
# - Why MobileNetV3-Large: its MACs are ~40% of our own CNN's and ~1/7 of ResNet-18's; so the three models
#   are at clearly different cost levels. Small is cheaper, but its capacity may be limited for the fine
#   facial details needed for age. EfficientNet-B0 is more expensive and uses the SiLU activation, which
#   runs slowly on a CPU.
# - The efficiency idea: depthwise separable convolutions (3x3 per channel + 1x1 mixing),
#   inverted residual blocks and squeeze-excitation; they do the same work with far fewer MACs.
# - Caveat: depthwise convolutions are memory-bound on a CPU; therefore the real time and energy may
#   not drop as much as the MACs. This difference will be seen in the measurement (CodeCarbon).
# - The architecture is not changed; only the last Linear layer of the classifier (1280 -> 1000) is
#   replaced with a single-output regression head. Training settings and input size are the same as the other models.

MOBILENET_RUN = "mobilenetv3_large_imagenet_64"


def build_mobilenet_v3_large():
    """MobileNetV3-Large with ImageNet weights + regression head."""
    backbone = mobilenet_v3_large(weights=MobileNet_V3_Large_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1)
    backbone.classifier[-1] = regression_head(backbone.classifier[-1].in_features)  # 1280 -> 1
    return AgeRegressor(backbone)


def train_mobilenet_v3_large():
    """Reports the size of MobileNetV3-Large, then trains and measures the model (or reads the saved result)."""
    parameters, macs = complexity(build_mobilenet_v3_large())
    print(f"MobileNetV3-Large (input {INPUT_SIZE}x{INPUT_SIZE}): {parameters:,} parameters, "
          f"{macs / 1e6:.1f} M MACs / image")
    return run_experiment(MOBILENET_RUN, build_mobilenet_v3_large, INPUT_SIZE)


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Put a regression head instead of the classifier head in both.
# =====================================================================================
# The same method in both models: the last classification layer (1000 outputs) is replaced with
# regression_head() (single-output Linear, bias = mean train age) and AgeRegressor makes the output (N,).
#     ResNet-18         : fc (512 -> 1000)              -> Linear(512 -> 1)
#     MobileNetV3-Large : classifier[-1] (1280 -> 1000) -> Linear(1280 -> 1)
# Check: both models return a single age prediction of shape (N,) for a sample input, and the initial
# prediction is close to the train mean (~33 years).


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Fine-tune at least one of them from ImageNet weights (transfer learning).
# =====================================================================================
# Both standard models are fine-tuned from ImageNet weights (torchvision IMAGENET1K_V1):
# build_resnet18() and build_mobilenet_v3_large() are built with weights=...IMAGENET1K_V1 and all
# layers (none frozen) are retrained for age regression. Since our own CNN is trained from scratch,
# the comparison also shows the effect of transfer learning.


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Discuss the carbon footprint that pretraining created in the past.
# =====================================================================================
# The ImageNet weights we use do not appear in our emissions.csv, but they are not free:
# someone trained them once and that energy was spent ("embodied carbon"). No energy / carbon value
# has been published for these weights, so it is estimated.
#
# Verified facts (sources):
#   - torchvision training recipe (references/classification/README.md):
#       "Except otherwise noted, all models have been trained on 8x V100 GPUs"
#       ResNet-18   : 90 epochs (general table and train.py default), batch 32 / GPU
#       MobileNetV3 : "--epochs 600 --opt rmsprop --batch-size 128 ..."
#     The README gives no training time, energy or carbon.
#   - MACs per image (224x224): torchvision weight metadata (_ops), ResNet-18 1.814 G,
#     MobileNetV3-Large 0.217 G. (Consistent with our 64x64 measurement: 148 M x (224/64)^2 ≈ 1.81 G.)
#   - The MobileNetV3 architecture was found by search (Howard et al., 2019, "Searching for MobileNetV3"):
#       "we use platform-aware NAS to search for the global network structures ...
#        We then use the NetAdapt algorithm to search per layer for the number of filters."
#     The paper does not give the search cost. MnasNet, which introduced the same search method (Tan et al., 2019):
#       "each architecture search takes 4.5 days on 64 TPUv2 devices ... our controller
#        samples about 8K models during architecture search"
#
# Estimation method (only the final published training run):
#   training FLOPs = 3 (forward + backward) x 2 (FLOP / MAC) x MACs x number of images x epochs
#   GPU-hours      = FLOPs / (GPU utilization x V100 FP32 peak throughput) / 3600
#   energy         = GPU-hours x GPU power x PUE (data-center overhead)
#   CO2            = energy x carbon intensity of the grid
# Since utilization, PUE and carbon intensity are unknown, three scenarios are used.

IMAGENET_TRAIN_IMAGES = 1_281_167
V100_FP32_TFLOPS = 15.7      # NVIDIA V100 peak FP32 throughput
V100_POWER_KW = 0.300        # V100 SXM2 TDP; the server's CPU/RAM power is not included (lower bound)

PRETRAINED_MODELS = [
    # (name, weights, number of ImageNet epochs, name of our fine-tuning run)
    ("ResNet-18", ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1, 90, RESNET_RUN),
    ("MobileNetV3-Large", MobileNet_V3_Large_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1, 600, MOBILENET_RUN),
]

PRETRAINING_SCENARIOS = [
    # (name, GPU utilization, PUE, carbon intensity kg CO2 / kWh)
    ("Optimistic", 0.40, 1.1, 0.2),
    ("Central", 0.20, 1.3, 0.4),
    ("Pessimistic", 0.10, 1.6, 0.6),
]

MNASNET_SEARCH_DEVICE_HOURS = 4.5 * 24 * 64   # 6912 TPUv2 device-hours (MnasNet paper)


def pretraining_estimate(macs_224, epochs, utilization, pue, carbon_intensity):
    """Estimate of the FLOPs, GPU-hours, kWh and kg CO2 of one ImageNet pretraining."""
    flops = 3 * 2 * macs_224 * IMAGENET_TRAIN_IMAGES * epochs
    gpu_hours = flops / (utilization * V100_FP32_TFLOPS * 1e12) / 3600
    energy_kwh = gpu_hours * V100_POWER_KW * pue
    return flops, gpu_hours, energy_kwh, energy_kwh * carbon_intensity


def load_summary(run_name):
    """Returns the saved summary of a run; None if the run has not been done yet."""
    path = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, f"{run_name}_summary.json")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as file:
        return json.load(file)


def report_pretraining_footprint():
    """Prints the estimated energy and CO2 of pretraining and compares them with our measurements."""
    rows = [["Model", "Epochs", "Training FLOPs", "Scenario", "GPU-hours", "Energy (kWh)", "CO2 (kg)"]]
    middle = {}
    for name, weights, epochs, _ in PRETRAINED_MODELS:
        macs_224 = weights.meta["_ops"] * 1e9
        for scenario, utilization, pue, intensity in PRETRAINING_SCENARIOS:
            flops, gpu_hours, kwh, co2 = pretraining_estimate(macs_224, epochs, utilization, pue, intensity)
            rows.append([name, epochs, f"{flops:.2e}", scenario, f"{gpu_hours:.0f}", f"{kwh:.1f}", f"{co2:.1f}"])
            if scenario == "Central":
                middle[name] = (kwh, co2)
    print_table("Estimated footprint of ImageNet pretraining (only the final published run):", rows)
    print("\nScenario assumptions (GPU utilization / PUE / kg CO2 per kWh):")
    for scenario, utilization, pue, intensity in PRETRAINING_SCENARIOS:
        print(f"  {scenario:11s}: {utilization * 100:.0f}% / {pue} / {intensity}")

    # Comparison with the fine-tuning trainings we measured
    rows = [["Model", "Pretraining (Central, kWh)", "Our fine-tuning (Wh)", "Pretraining / fine-tuning"]]
    ratios = []
    for name, _, _, run_name in PRETRAINED_MODELS:
        summary = load_summary(run_name)
        if summary is None:
            rows.append([name, f"{middle[name][0]:.1f}", "not trained yet", "-"])
        else:
            ratios.append(middle[name][0] * 1000 / summary["train_energy_Wh"])
            rows.append([name, f"{middle[name][0]:.1f}", f"{summary['train_energy_Wh']:.2f}", f"~{ratios[-1]:,.0f}x"])
    print_table("Pretraining vs. the fine-tuning energy we measured:", rows)
    scale = f"~{min(ratios):,.0f}-{max(ratios):,.0f} times" if ratios else "(fine-tuning not measured yet)"

    print(f"""
Discussion:
  1) Scale: in the central scenario, a single ImageNet pretraining consumes {scale} more energy
     than one of our fine-tuning trainings. By downloading the weights we do not repeat this cost;
     we only pay a very small fine-tuning cost. This is the green side of transfer learning.
  2) This estimate is a lower bound. It counts only the final published training run; hyperparameter
     searches, failed trials and development runs are not included. Also only GPU power is counted
     (no server CPU, RAM and network power) and the carbon of hardware manufacturing is not included.
  3) An "efficient model" is efficient at inference, not at training. MobileNetV3-Large does ~8 times
     fewer MACs per image than ResNet-18, but since it was trained for 600 instead of 90 epochs the total
     training compute is almost the same. Because depthwise convolutions use the GPU less efficiently and
     600 epochs of data augmentation load the CPU, its real cost is most likely closer to the
     pessimistic scenario.
  4) The cost of the architecture search must be added separately. The MobileNetV3 architecture was found
     with a MnasNet-style search and NetAdapt. According to the MnasNet paper a single search takes 4.5 days
     on 64 TPUv2 devices: {MNASNET_SEARCH_DEVICE_HOURS:,.0f} device-hours, i.e. far more than the GPU-hours of
     the weight training above. The MobileNetV3 paper does not give its own search cost, so it can only be
     given as an order of magnitude. ResNet, on the other hand, was designed by hand.
  5) Sharing (amortization): pretraining is done once and the weights are reused by many people; the share
     per person is small. However, an honest carbon report of the project should state this embodied cost
     separately, as an estimate, next to the emissions.csv total.
  6) The uncertainty is large: there is a ~{max_min_ratio():.0f}x difference between the scenarios. Therefore
     the result should be reported not as a single number but as a range and an order of magnitude.""")


def max_min_ratio():
    """Ratio between the pessimistic and optimistic scenario CO2 estimates (independent of the model)."""
    estimates = [pretraining_estimate(1.0, 1, u, p, c)[3] for _, u, p, c in PRETRAINING_SCENARIOS]
    return max(estimates) / min(estimates)


# =====================================================================================
# [x] Use the same split, the same image size policy and the same evaluation code for all models.
# =====================================================================================
# How it is ensured in code:
#   - Same split : every model reads data/splits.csv with data_utils.load_split() (seed 42,
#                  generated once and preserved). The test set only in step 5, with load_test_once().
#   - Same images: every model gets the same 200x200 -> 64x64 bilinear-downscaled images from the same
#                  cache (data_utils.load_images) and the same normalization computed from train.
#   - Same code  : every model is trained and measured with train_utils.run_experiment(): same loss,
#                  optimizer, lr, schedule, augmentation, stopping, the same regression_metrics()
#                  and the same CodeCarbon measurement. The only model-specific part is the build_model function.
# check_fairness() verifies this on the runs that were executed and shows the results in one table.

COMPARED_RUNS = [
    # (name, run name, pretraining)
    ("Own CNN", "own_cnn_64", "none (from scratch)"),
    ("ResNet-18", RESNET_RUN, "ImageNet"),
    ("MobileNetV3-Large", MOBILENET_RUN, "ImageNet"),
]
OWN_CNN_LAYERS_CSV = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "own_cnn_layers.csv")
MODEL_BUILDERS = {RESNET_RUN: build_resnet18, MOBILENET_RUN: build_mobilenet_v3_large}


RUN_NOTES_CSV = os.path.join(ROOT, "emissions", "run_notes.csv")


def measurement_status(run_name):
    """Status of the training measurement used in the run's summary (emissions/run_notes.csv)."""
    if not os.path.exists(RUN_NOTES_CSV):
        return "no note (ran alone)"
    notes = pd.read_csv(RUN_NOTES_CSV)
    used = notes[(notes["project_name"] == run_name) & (notes["used_in_summary"] == "yes")]
    if used.empty:
        return "no note (ran alone)"
    note = used.iloc[-1]
    return f"{note['measurement_status']}, {note['power_mode']}"


def file_fingerprint(path):
    """First 12 characters of the file's SHA-256 digest."""
    with open(path, "rb") as file:
        return hashlib.sha256(file.read()).hexdigest()[:12]


def run_macs(run_name):
    """MACs per image at 64x64 of the run's model."""
    if run_name in MODEL_BUILDERS:
        return complexity(MODEL_BUILDERS[run_name]())[1]
    return pd.read_csv(OWN_CNN_LAYERS_CSV)["MACs"].sum()  # own CNN: the layer table of step 2


def check_fairness():
    """Verifies that all models were evaluated with the same split, the same input size and the same code."""
    split_time = os.path.getmtime(SPLITS_CSV)
    print(f"Split file    : {SPLITS_CSV}")
    print(f"  SHA-256     : {file_fingerprint(SPLITS_CSV)}   (all models read this file)")
    print(f"  Last change : {datetime.fromtimestamp(split_time):%Y-%m-%d %H:%M}")
    print(f"Training settings (train_utils, identical for all models): batch {BATCH_SIZE}, AdamW lr {LEARNING_RATE:g}, "
          f"weight decay {WEIGHT_DECAY:g}, early stopping {EARLY_STOP_PATIENCE}. The epoch limit per model is "
          f"in the table (current setting: {MAX_EPOCHS}).")

    rows = [["Model", "Pretraining", "Input", "Epoch limit", "Split before training?", "Params", "MACs (M)",
             "val MAE", "val RMSE", "val R²", "Training (Wh)", "Inference (mWh/1000)", "Energy measurement"]]
    problems, epoch_limits = [], set()
    for name, run_name, pretraining in COMPARED_RUNS:
        summary = load_summary(run_name)
        if summary is None:
            rows.append([name, pretraining, "-", "-", "-", "-", "-", "not trained yet", "", "", "", "", ""])
            problems.append(f"{name} not trained yet")
            continue

        summary_time = os.path.getmtime(os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, f"{run_name}_summary.json"))
        split_before = summary_time > split_time
        if summary["input_size"] != INPUT_SIZE:
            problems.append(f"{name}: input {summary['input_size']} (expected {INPUT_SIZE})")
        if not split_before:
            problems.append(f"{name}: the split file changed after this training")

        # The "max_epochs" field was added to the summary later; all summaries without it were trained with a 20-epoch limit.
        epoch_limit = summary.get("max_epochs", 20)
        epoch_limits.add(epoch_limit)
        rows.append([name, pretraining, f"{summary['input_size']}px", epoch_limit,
                     "yes" if split_before else "NO",
                     f"{summary['parameters']:,}", f"{run_macs(run_name) / 1e6:.1f}",
                     f"{summary['val_MAE']:.2f}", f"{summary['val_RMSE']:.2f}", f"{summary['val_R2']:.3f}",
                     f"{summary['train_energy_Wh']:.2f}", f"{summary['infer_mWh_per_1000']:.2f}",
                     measurement_status(run_name)])
    print_table("Results measured with the same split, the same input and the same code (validation):", rows)
    if any(word in row[-1] for row in rows[1:] for word in ("overlapping", "sleep", "low (")):
        print("\nWarning: the energy measurements were not taken under the same conditions (overlapping runs /\n"
              f"different power modes); details in {RUN_NOTES_CSV}. The error metrics (val MAE, RMSE, R²) are not affected.")

    if len(epoch_limits) > 1:
        problems.append(f"the models were trained with different epoch limits ({sorted(epoch_limits)}); "
                        "the training budget is not equal, this must be stated in the report")

    if problems:
        print("\nMissing / inconsistent:")
        for problem in problems:
            print(f"  - {problem}")
    else:
        print("\nCheck passed: all models were measured with the same split, the same 64x64 input and the same "
              "training/evaluation code.")


def main():
    print_section("1) Large model: ResNet-18 (ImageNet fine-tuning)")
    train_resnet18()

    print_section("2) Efficiency-oriented model: MobileNetV3-Large (ImageNet fine-tuning)")
    train_mobilenet_v3_large()

    print_section("3) Carbon footprint of pretraining")
    report_pretraining_footprint()

    print_section("4) Same split, same image size and same evaluation code")
    check_fairness()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

+# Chosen: ResNet-18, fine-tuned from ImageNet weights (torchvision IMAGENET1K_V1).
+# - Why ResNet-18: the smallest standard representative of the "large model" class that can be trained
+#   on a CPU. With 11.2 M parameters it is about 38 times larger than our own CNN (~0.29 M); ResNet-50 (25.6 M)
+#   or ConvNeXt-Tiny (28.6 M) would take hours on this machine (no GPU) and consume much more energy.
+# - The architecture is not changed (so it stays a standard model): only the last layer (fc, 1000 classes)
+#   is replaced with a single-output regression head.
+# - With a 64x64 input, ResNet's stem (stride-2 conv + max pool) and the following stages shrink the map
+#   to 2x2; this is a known cost of the shared image size policy.
+# - The training settings (loss, optimizer, lr, schedule, augmentation, stopping) are the same as for our
+#   own CNN. The input normalization is also the same (computed from the train set); using it instead of the
+#   ImageNet statistics is acceptable because the BN layers adapt during fine-tuning.
+# - The weights are downloaded while the model is built, before the energy measurement starts.

+# - Why MobileNetV3-Large: its MACs are ~40% of our own CNN's and ~1/7 of ResNet-18's; so the three models

+#   facial details needed for age. EfficientNet-B0 is more expensive and uses the SiLU activation, which
+# - The efficiency idea: depthwise separable convolutions (3x3 per channel + 1x1 mixing),

239	def model_size(build_model, input_size, checkpoint_path):
240	    """(parametre, MFLOPs / görüntü, ağırlık dosyası MB, checkpoint dosyası MB)."""
241	    model = build_model().eval()
242	    parameters = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
243	    with FlopCounterMode(display=False) as counter, torch.no_grad():
244	        model(torch.zeros(1, 3, input_size, input_size))
245	
246	    state = torch.load(checkpoint_path, weights_only=False)["model_state"]
247	    buffer = io.BytesIO()
248	    torch.save(state, buffer)
249	    return (parameters, counter.get_total_flops() / 1e6, buffer.getbuffer().nbytes / 1024 ** 2,
250	            os.path.getsize(checkpoint_path) / 1024 ** 2)

306	# [x] Ayak izini azaltmak için en az birkaç teknik dene (küçük çözünürlük, early stopping,
307	#     mixed precision, veriyi cache'leme, alt küme üzerinde LR araması vb.) ve ne kadar
308	#     tasarruf sağladığını raporla.
309	# =====================================================================================
310	# Beş teknik denenir. Var olan koşulara dokunulmaz; yeni ölçümler kısa tutulur, emissions.csv'ye
311	# "reduce_" önekiyle yazılır ve hepsi aynı oturumda arka arkaya yapılır (aynı güç modu, başka yük
312	# yok). Sonuçlar models/reduction/reduction_results.json'a kaydedilir; dosya varsa ölçümler
313	# tekrarlanmaz.

320	#                         Önbellek olmasaydı bu iş her epoch'ta tekrarlanırdı.
321	#   4) Alt küme LR ar.  : 3 öğrenme oranı train setinin %20'sinde 3'er epoch denenir. Tüm veride
322	#                         20 epoch'luk bir aramanın enerjisi, aynı oturumdaki ölçümden
323	#                         (görüntü-epoch başına enerji) tahmin edilir.
324	#   5) Early stopping   : yeni koşu yoktur. Final koşuların epoch geçmişinden, farklı sabır
325	#                         değerleriyle eğitimin nerede duracağı ve ne kadar enerji kalacağı
326	#                         geriye dönük hesaplanır (LR schedule durmadan önceki epoch'larda aynıdır,
327	#                         bu yüzden hesap kesindir). 48px koşusu uyku arası nedeniyle dahil edilmez.
328	
329	REDUCTION_DIR = os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, "reduction")
330	REDUCTION_JSON = os.path.join(REDUCTION_DIR, "reduction_results.json")
331	LR_CANDIDATES = [3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3]
332	LR_SUBSET_FRACTION = 0.2
333	LR_SEARCH_EPOCHS = 3
334	PATIENCE_OPTIONS = [3, 5, EARLY_STOP_PATIENCE]
335	EARLY_STOP_RUNS = [("Kendi CNN", "own_cnn_64"), ("ResNet-18", standard.RESNET_RUN),
336	                   ("MobileNetV3-Large", standard.MOBILENET_RUN)]
337	
338	
339	def measure_own_cnn_inference(label, run_name, input_size, bfloat16=False):
340	    """Kendi CNN'in final modeliyle val setini INFERENCE_REPEATS kez tahmin eder ve ölçer."""
341	    val = load_split("val")
342	    saved = torch.load(os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, f"{run_name}.pt"), weights_only=False)
343	    model = own_cnn.AgeCNN()
344	    model.load_state_dict(saved["model_state"])
345	    images = torch.from_numpy(load_images(val, input_size, "val"))
346	
347	    def run():
348	        precision = torch.autocast("cpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16) if bfloat16 else contextlib.nullcontext()
349	        with precision:
350	            return [predict(model, images, saved["mean"], saved["std"]) for _ in range(INFERENCE_REPEATS)][0]
351	
352	    predictions, energy = measure_energy(label, run)
353	    return {"energy_Wh": energy["energy_Wh"], "seconds": energy["seconds"],
354	            "val_MAE": regression_metrics(val["age"], predictions)["MAE"]}
355	
356	
357	def measure_caching():
358	    """Bir epoch'luk train verisini önbelleksiz (JPEG çözme) ve önbellekten hazırlamayı ölçer."""
359	    train = load_split("train")
360	    _, no_cache = measure_energy("reduce_cache_off_decode_jpeg", lambda: decode_images(train, 64))
361	    _, cache = measure_energy("reduce_cache_on_load_npz", lambda: load_images(train, 64, "train"))
362	    return {"no_cache": no_cache, "cache": cache}
363	
364	
365	def lr_search_on_subset():
366	    """Train setinin %20'sinde, her LR için LR_SEARCH_EPOCHS epoch kısa eğitim yapar ve ölçer."""
367	    train, val, train_images, val_images, mean, std = load_train_val(64)
368	    positions = np.sort(np.random.default_rng(SEED).choice(
369	        len(train), size=int(LR_SUBSET_FRACTION * len(train)), replace=False))
370	    subset = (train.iloc[positions].reset_index(drop=True), val,
371	              train_images[torch.from_numpy(positions)], val_images, mean, std)
372	
373	    results = []
374	    for lr in LR_CANDIDATES:
375	        model = own_cnn.build_own_cnn()
376	        name = f"reduce_lr_search_subset_lr{lr:g}"
377	        summary, energy = measure_energy(name, lambda: train_model(
378	            model, subset, os.path.join(REDUCTION_DIR, f"{name}.pt"),
379	            os.path.join(REDUCTION_DIR, f"{name}_history.csv"),
380	            learning_rate=lr, max_epochs=LR_SEARCH_EPOCHS))
381	        results.append({"lr": lr, "val_MAE": summary["val_MAE"], **energy})
382	    return {"subset_size": len(positions), "train_size": len(train), "runs": results}
383	
384	
385	def run_reduction_measurements():
386	    """Yeni ölçümleri bir kez, arka arkaya yapar; sonuçları JSON'a yazar (varsa okur)."""
387	    if os.path.exists(REDUCTION_JSON):
388	        print(f"Kayıtlı ölçümler kullanılıyor: {REDUCTION_JSON}")
389	        with open(REDUCTION_JSON, encoding="utf-8") as file:
390	            return json.load(file)
391	
392	    os.makedirs(REDUCTION_DIR, exist_ok=True)
393	    load_images(load_split("val"), 48, "val")  # önbellek hazır olsun; ölçüme karışmasın
394	    results = {
395	        "resolution_64": measure_own_cnn_inference("reduce_infer_own_cnn_64_fp32", "own_cnn_64", 64),
396	        "resolution_48": measure_own_cnn_inference("reduce_infer_own_cnn_48_fp32", "own_cnn_48", 48),
397	        "bfloat16_64": measure_own_cnn_inference("reduce_infer_own_cnn_64_bf16", "own_cnn_64", 64, True),
398	        "caching": measure_caching(),
399	        "lr_search": lr_search_on_subset(),
400	    }
401	    with open(REDUCTION_JSON, "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
402	        json.dump(results, file, indent=2)
403	    return results
404	
405	
406	def simulate_early_stopping(history, patience):
407	    """Geçmişe göre verilen sabırla eğitimin duracağı epoch'u ve o ana kadarki en iyi MAE'yi döndürür."""
408	    best, waited = float("inf"), 0
409	    for _, row in history.iterrows():
410	        if row["val_MAE"] < best:
411	            best, waited = row["val_MAE"], 0
412	        else:
413	            waited += 1
414	            if waited >= patience:
415	                return int(row["epoch"]), best
416	    return int(history["epoch"].iloc[-1]), best
417	
418	
419	def report_reductions(emissions):
420	    """Beş tekniğin tasarrufunu yazdırır."""
421	    results = run_reduction_measurements()
422	
423	    def change(new, old):
424	        return f"{100 * (new - old) / old:+.1f}%"
425	
426	    # 1-2) Çözünürlük ve mixed precision (çıkarım, aynı oturumda ölçüldü)
427	    base, small, bf16 = results["resolution_64"], results["resolution_48"], results["bfloat16_64"]
428	    n_predictions = len(load_split("val")) * INFERENCE_REPEATS
429	    rows = [["Varyant", "Enerji (Wh / 1000 tahmin)", "Gecikme (ms / görüntü)", "val MAE", "Enerji değişimi"]]
430	    for name, result in [("64px fp32 (temel)", base), ("48px fp32", small), ("64px bfloat16", bf16)]:
431	        rows.append([name, f"{1e3 * result['energy_Wh'] / n_predictions:.4f}",
432	                     f"{1e3 * result['seconds'] / n_predictions:.3f}", f"{result['val_MAE']:.2f}",
433	                     "-" if result is base else change(result["energy_Wh"], base["energy_Wh"])])
434	    print_table("1-2) Küçük çözünürlük ve mixed precision (kendi CNN, çıkarım, aynı oturum):", rows)
435	
436	    # 3) Cache'leme
437	    no_cache, cache = results["caching"]["no_cache"], results["caching"]["cache"]
438	    final_epochs = sum(len(pd.read_csv(os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, f"{run}_history.csv")))
439	                       for _, run in EARLY_STOP_RUNS)  # 64px final koşuların toplam epoch sayısı
440	    saved_wh = (no_cache["energy_Wh"] - cache["energy_Wh"]) * final_epochs
441	    rows = [["Veri hazırlama (1 epoch, train)", "Süre (sn)", "Enerji (Wh)"],
442	            ["JPEG çözme + küçültme (önbelleksiz)", f"{no_cache['seconds']:.1f}", f"{no_cache['energy_Wh']:.3f}"],
443	            ["Önbellekten okuma (.npz)", f"{cache['seconds']:.1f}", f"{cache['energy_Wh']:.3f}"]]
444	    print_table("3) Veriyi cache'leme:", rows)
445	    print(f"  Önbellek olmasaydı 64px final koşularının {final_epochs} epoch'unda fazladan "
446	          f"~{saved_wh:.1f} Wh harcanırdı (epoch başına {no_cache['energy_Wh'] - cache['energy_Wh']:.3f} Wh).")
447	
448	    # 4) Alt küme üzerinde LR araması
449	    search = results["lr_search"]
450	    rows = [["LR", f"val MAE ({LR_SEARCH_EPOCHS} epoch, %{100 * LR_SUBSET_FRACTION:.0f} veri)",
451	             "Süre (dk)", "Enerji (Wh)"]]
452	    for run in search["runs"]:
453	        rows.append([f"{run['lr']:g}", f"{run['val_MAE']:.2f}", f"{run['seconds'] / 60:.1f}", f"{run['energy_Wh']:.2f}"])
454	    subset_wh = sum(run["energy_Wh"] for run in search["runs"])
455	    wh_per_image_epoch = subset_wh / (search["subset_size"] * LR_SEARCH_EPOCHS * len(search["runs"]))
456	    full_wh = wh_per_image_epoch * search["train_size"] * MAX_EPOCHS * len(search["runs"])
457	    best_lr = min(search["runs"], key=lambda run: run["val_MAE"])["lr"]
458	    print_table("4) Alt küme üzerinde LR araması (kendi CNN, 64px):", rows)
459	    print(f"""  Seçilen LR: {best_lr:g} (final eğitimlerde kullanılan: {LEARNING_RATE:g})
460	  Alt küme araması: {subset_wh:.2f} Wh ölçüldü. Tüm veride {MAX_EPOCHS} epoch'luk aynı arama
461	  ≈ {full_wh:.1f} Wh tutardı (aynı oturumdaki görüntü-epoch başına enerjiden tahmin) -> tasarruf %{100 * (1 - subset_wh / full_wh):.1f}.
462	  Sınırlama: {LR_SEARCH_EPOCHS} epoch ve %{100 * LR_SUBSET_FRACTION:.0f} veriyle yapılan sıralama, uzun eğitimdeki
463	  sıralamanın yalnızca yaklaşık bir göstergesidir.""")
464	
465	    # 5) Early stopping (geriye dönük, mevcut geçmişlerden)
466	    rows = [["Model", "Sabır", "Durduğu epoch", "Kalan epoch", "Enerji tasarrufu", "val MAE (en iyi)", "MAE değişimi"]]
467	    for name, run in EARLY_STOP_RUNS:
468	        history = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(MODEL_DIR, f"{run}_history.csv"))
469	        energy_wh = used_row(emissions, run)["energy_consumed"] * 1000
470	        full_best = history["val_MAE"].min()
471	        for patience in PATIENCE_OPTIONS:
472	            stop_epoch, best = simulate_early_stopping(history, patience)
473	            remaining = history[history["epoch"] > stop_epoch]["seconds"].sum() / history["seconds"].sum()
474	            rows.append([name, patience, stop_epoch, len(history) - stop_epoch,
475	                         f"%{100 * remaining:.0f} ({energy_wh * remaining:.1f} Wh)",
476	                         f"{best:.2f}", f"{best - full_best:+.2f}"])
477	    print_table(f"5) Early stopping (geriye dönük; şu anki ayar sabır {EARLY_STOP_PATIENCE}, "
478	                f"en fazla {MAX_EPOCHS} epoch):", rows)
479	    print(f"""  Sabır {EARLY_STOP_PATIENCE} (şu anki ayar) satırları koşuların gerçekte durduğu epoch'u gösterir; durduğu epoch
480	  koşulan son epoch'a eşitse eğitimi erken durdurma değil epoch üst sınırı bitirmiştir.
481	  Daha küçük sabır eğitimi erken keser ve enerji kazandırır, ama en iyi epoch'u kaçırma
482	  riski vardır (MAE değişimi sütunu). Enerji, epoch sürelerine göre orantılanarak hesaplanmıştır.""")
483	
484	
485	def main():
486	    # Ayak izi azaltma ölçümleri (yalnızca ilk çalıştırmada) en başta yapılır; böylece aşağıdaki
487	    # toplam tablosu bu yeni koşuları da içerir.
488	    run_reduction_measurements()
489	    emissions = read_emissions()
490	
491	    print_section("1) Final eğitimlerin enerjisi, süre, boyut ve çıkarım maliyeti (model başına)")
492	    report_models(emissions)
493	
494	    print_section("2) Projenin toplam enerjisi ve emisyonu")
495	    runs = report_project_total(emissions)
496	
497	    print_section("2b) Ölçüm oturumlarının karşılaştırması (Windows ayarları öncesi / sonrası)")
498	    report_session_comparison(runs)
499	
500	    print_section("3) Donanım ve konum")
501	    report_hardware(emissions)
502	
503	    print_section("4) Ayak izini azaltma teknikleri")

505	
506
